title: Analytics pillar — video 04 talking-point and screen rubric
note: Scored by gen-ceo-video-review.js --pillar analytics. `judge_on: auto` criteria are measured by the deterministic probes in generators/lib/rubric-review.js and must not be supplied as verdicts. `screen` criteria are judged on the panels the deck embeds and need a `ref` (story#scN:panel.png). Evidence quoted only from an `also` story caps a narration verdict at partial. Keep ids stable: past verdicts bind to them.

scale.covered: Stated explicitly and clearly enough that a first-time viewer would take the point away.
scale.partial: Touched, implied, or named without enough substance to land — a viewer could miss it.
scale.missed: Not present in the narration at all.

weights.must: The video fails its job without this.
weights.should: Expected; its absence is a real gap worth fixing before the next cut.
weights.nice: Strengthens the story; acceptable to trade away for time.

dimensions.name: Analytics — governed products people act on
dimensions.framing: The apps, Answers and Predict read the governed gold products, and somebody at Meridian decides something differently because of them. Insight that stops at the insight is unfinished.

criteria.name: Every scene shows a real tenant capture
criteria.expect: Each scene of the Analytics video embeds a qlik_panels/*.png captured from the live tenant. No drawn chart (QlikApp.app / barSvg), no missing file, no panel edited after capture.

criteria.name: The app load scripts read the warehouse, not files
criteria.expect: The app load scripts read the gold and silver tables over a warehouse/lakehouse SQL connection (LIB CONNECT + SELECT FROM schema.table), not lib:// .qvd or .csv files on a connection named after the lakehouse.
criteria.source: plan § B 'Apps read Gold from Snowflake'; deploy/apps/load-scripts/app1-supply-chain.qvs:61, app2-delivery-experience.qvs:64

criteria.name: The panels show the live sheets and surfaces
criteria.expect: The sheets, Answers and Predict scenes show the real app sheets, the Answers response with its citation visible, and the configured Predict experiment — live captures that match the narration, not a drawn chart or a panel reused from another story.

criteria.name: The apps read the two gold data products
criteria.expect: The narration says the apps are built on the two gold data products — Supply Chain Health and Last Mile Performance — not on a separate extract.

criteria.name: One worked decision, made by a named role
criteria.expect: At least one worked example in which a named role — the EU Logistics Manager, a DC manager, the APAC logistics lead — decides something differently because of what the app shows: the decision and the outcome, not only the insight.

criteria.name: Predict on governed data, honestly labelled
criteria.expect: Predict is trained on the same governed data, and its output is presented as what the model is built to find or expected to confirm — not as a finding already proven.

criteria.name: Automations detect, notify and correct — with a recipient
criteria.expect: An automation detects a condition, notifies a named person or role, and triggers the correction: a recipient, not just 'the operations channel'.

criteria.name: A number moves against the $127M baseline
criteria.expect: A measure moves against the baseline — inventory record accuracy, delivery promise accuracy, WISMO volume, or dollars of the $127M — a claim of value, not only of capability.

criteria.name: Alerts reach a named person
criteria.expect: A Discovery Agent or app alert reaches a named person or role who acts on it.

criteria.name: Forward-looking and preview are labelled aloud
criteria.expect: Anything forward-looking or preview — sheet authoring over the MCP server, findings a model is expected to confirm — is labelled as such in the narration.
criteria.source: MCG_Agentic_Data_Engineering.md § GA vs preview status; agentic-video-rubric.json AAX-10
